text:
mike_sales: Hey team — hyperscale bank POC question. They want Redwood Private deployed into their VPC with model traffic egressing to their on‑prem SNI proxy. Need to confirm firewall rules, source IP requirements, and any visibility/cost notes we should flag to procurement.

anita_netops: Quick clarifying q: for the flow, will model inference connections originate from our infra into their proxy (outbound from Redwood), or should their network initiate connections into our VPC?

mike_sales: Outbound from Redwood -> their on‑prem proxy. They require SNI to be preserved so their TLS terminator can route to backends. Also they asked for source IP preservation.

dave_sre: Ok. Source IP preservation means static egress IPs (EIPs) or a customer NAT solution. Options: (1) assign EIPs to NAT Gateway(s) in their VPC for preserved source, or (2) place a small TGW/NAT in our account with advertised static IPs — both have tradeoffs.

anita_netops: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering note: PrivateLink is good for inbound API endpoints (reduces exposure), but it doesn't change outbound egress behavior. Peering can introduce asymmetric routing if they NAT on their side. Recommend PrivateLink for control-plane/API ingress + customer-managed egress for model traffic to their proxy.

sarah_solutions: Procurement also asked about incremental charges: are there per-endpoint costs, per-GB, and any additional networking fees we should surface?

dave_sre: Yes — cloud charges: interface endpoint hourly + data processing, EIP allocation fees (depending on provider), NAT GW per-hour + data transfer. Also cross‑region egress if traffic crosses regions. We'll give a ballpark.

mike_sales: Can we get a concise firewall rule snippet I can paste to their netops? They want explicit allow rules they can drop into their firewall ticket.

dave_sre: Sure. Example minimal rules (they'll adapt to their CIDR/IP naming):
```
# Outbound from Redwood subnets to customer on-prem proxy
allow tcp 10.0.0.0/22 -> 203.0.113.45:443  # model traffic to customer proxy (SNI preserved)
# Inbound to Redwood health endpoints (management/agent checks)
allow tcp 198.51.100.10 -> 10.0.0.0/22:443  # Redwood health / metrics
# DNS and NTP (if needed)
allow udp 10.0.0.0/22 -> 8.8.8.8:53
allow udp 10.0.0.0/22 -> 169.254.169.123:123
```
Note: replace 203.0.113.45 with their proxy IP(s), and 198.51.100.10 with our management IPs (we'll supply exact list).

security_bot: Security checklist: request from customer SOC/infosec — 1) confirm KMS/HSM key handling for any customer secrets, 2) audit log retention window, 3) TLS mutual auth requirements, 4) confirmation that SNI is not rewritten by their proxy, 5) whether PCI/SO DLP applies to payloads.

anita_netops: For SNI specifically — our client preserves SNI by default. Important: if their TLS terminator does SNI rewrite, routing fails. Ask them to validate SNI passthrough to backend or give us the rewritten host header.

mike_sales: They also want to know if PrivateLink endpoints can be used instead of exposing public EIPs for management traffic — are there limitations?

dave_sre: PrivateLink is fine for management/control-plane endpoints. It reduces the need for public IPs for that traffic. However, any egress that must go to their on‑prem proxy will still traverse the outbound path and require static egress handling if they want source preservation.

sarah_solutions: I'll draft the cost estimate: PrivateLink endpoint pricing + per‑GB for endpoint data, NAT/EIP costs, and any cross‑region egress. Will share a 3‑line summary for procurement.

mike_sales: Can someone capture a short preflight checklist I can send to their NetOps + Security teams? Need it in next 2 hours.

anita_netops: I'll post a checklist in 45m. It will include: required IP allowlist (we'll list our management IPs), ports (443 outbound to proxy, 443 inbound for health), SNI note, static EIP options, IAM roles for endpoint creation, and a short cost pointer. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reminder — if we provision interface endpoints in their account, we need the endpoint service name + VPC ID + subnet IDs before we start.

mike_sales: Perfect — thanks all. I'll wait for the checklist and the cost ballpark to share with the customer. :pray:
